subject: Isolated original-client S5 rock-slope route revision stops at its first local waypoint
scope: One copied-client 1.16.5.0 diagnostic using the ordinary copied Game DLL and archived post-Conrad-corpse character database. Only the copied mission 1995 objective 1 timer anchor was reset. This was not a continuous original-timer run.

exact_locations: output/driver-second-sandbag.log: move 10 and move 11 lines through final RuntimeError

observations.finding: The client traversed ordinary movement to pre-route waypoint 10, reaching (-164.78906, 88.34375, -13.7421875), then climbed toward the first inserted local point (-168.54297, 91.46875, -16.929688). Three accepted moves reached (-167.99219, 90.56641, -15.964844).
observations.source_location: output/driver-second-sandbag.log move 10 and move 11 lines; output/positions.tsv final rows

observations.finding: From (-167.99219, 90.56641, -15.964844), the next forward hold yielded accepted positions (-168.9375, 90.35156, -15.453125) and (-170.3711, 90.81641, -15.8984375). Relative to the first local target, the driver computed target progress -0.417 m and -0.988 m. Its eight-second positive-progress guard stopped the attempt at waypoint 11 before any second sandbag or bomb interaction.
observations.source_location: output/driver-second-sandbag.log final RuntimeError; output/positions.tsv final two rows

observations.finding: A screenshot before the final accepted moves shows the player on a rocky slope with the mission timer at 06:03 and the target wreck/sandbag area farther ahead. The screenshot does not establish an impassable collision or original final-live intended route.

The detached supervisor ended after 225.17 seconds because the driver exited 1. It issued a normal stop command, the isolated launcher exited 0, and output/status.json recorded terminal copied Auth, Game, display and client processes. The earlier supervisor shutdown race did not recur.

The copied database remained SQLite-integrity ok with mission 1995 active, objective 1 active, and objectives 2 and 3 complete. Its saved character position remained the initial checkpoint, so the accepted movement positions must be read from the trace rather than the character row.

assessment.finding: The fixed first local target and yaw adjustment did not reproduce the earlier accepted climb sequence from a slightly different approach position. The negative target progress is a controller route divergence, not proof that the game path is blocked. A future attempt would need a locally adaptive heading or a closer matched approach position under the same accepted-Move and timer guards.

unverified: A client-controlled route past the rocky slope and second wreck sandbag
